title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC1LD_0RA0LD_1LB0LA_1RF1RA_---1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC1LD_0RA0LD_1LB0LA_1RF1RA_---1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced exactly to a question about numbers. Lean proves (kernel) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (0, 5) under an explicit map next on pairs of numbers reaches none (halts_iff, lean/Macro.lean). The orbit passes through the rounds with fuel 5, 14 and 185 without halting; the fourth round has fuel 22,205,951,667,644,132,025,548 and decides on the parity of a 3/2-map iterated about 1022 times, out of reach of any computation. Heuristically each round halts with probability about 1/3, so the machine probably halts, but after a number of steps with about 1021 digits.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,446 cells have been visited and 29,592 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The rules of a round
claims.text: Ten rules on symbolic tapes, each for all values of its variables: start (blank tape to D(0,0,5) in 136 steps), d_step (D(k+1,y,z) to D(k,y+3,z)), d_zero (D(0,y,z) to A(y+3,z)), a_odd, a_odd_one, a_even, a_even_two (A to D using fuel), reset_odd, reset_even (out of fuel: the block becomes the new fuel) and halt_even (out of fuel with an even block: halt).

claims.title: Halting is the orbit of a map
claims.text: With next k z: for k even, (3(k/2)+1, z-1) if z ≥ 1 and (0, 3(k/2)+2) if z = 0; for k odd, (3(k/2)+4, z-2) if z ≥ 2, (0, 3(k/2)+5) if z = 1, and none (halt) if z = 0: the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (0, 5) under next reaches none.

claims.title: Three rounds survive
claims.text: The orbit from (0, 5) resets with fuel 14, then 185, then 22,205,951,667,644,132,025,548 (138 applications of next), without halting. In the real run the tape shows fuel 14 at step 653 and fuel 185 at step 59,197.

claims.title: Each round halts with chance about 1/3
claims.text: Every round starts at k = 0, so the sequence of k values is the same in every round; only the fuel z decides where it stops. Writing u = k + 2 the sequence is u → 3⌈u/2⌉ from u = 2, and a round with fuel z halts exactly when z equals the fuel spent before some odd u. For z up to 20,000 that is 33.6% of the values. If the reset values behave like random numbers, the machine halts with probability 1, in some round after the third.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: equivalent to whether 22,205,951,667,644,132,025,548 or a later reset value lands on an odd point of the u-sequence. Deciding even the fourth round needs the parity of u<sub>i</sub> for i near 1.5·10<sup>22</sup>, a problem of the same kind as the open Hydra and Antihydra questions.

explainer.lede: Probably yes, but nobody can check it. The machine runs a 3/2-Collatz-like map that burns a fuel counter; when the fuel runs out it either halts or turns its current number into new, enormously larger fuel. It has survived three rounds. The fourth has 22,205,951,667,644,132,025,548 units of fuel.

facts.text: An exact reduction to a map on pairs of numbers, proved in Lean.
The fuel of the first four rounds.
Chance that a round ends in a halt.
No halt in the C simulator; 49,446 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Two blocks and a fuel tank
html: After a short start, the tape always looks like one of two shapes (written left to right, (01)^k is k copies of 01, S> the head in state S on the next cell):

nametape
D(k, y, z)0∞ (01)^(k+1) D> 1^(y+1) (10)^z 1 0∞
A(m, z)0∞ A> 1^m (10)^z 1 0∞
The block (10)^z on the right is fuel: it is only ever shortened, by one or two copies per round. The left block holds a number k that is multiplied by about 3/2 each time.

sections.heading: Times three, halve, burn fuel
html: All of these are proved in Lean for every value of the variables (lean/Rules.lean, lean/Macro.lean):

fromtowhat happens
D(k+1, y, z)D(k, y+3, z)one 01 on the left becomes three 1s on the right (d_step)
D(0, y, z)A(y+3, z)the left block is empty: A starts at the left end (d_zero)
A(2i+1, z+1)D(i, 0, z)A halves an odd block and burns one unit of fuel
A(2i+2, z+2)D(i+2, 0, z)an even block: two units of fuel
A(2i+1, 0)D(0, 0, i+1)no fuel: the block becomes the new fuel (reset)
A(2i+2, 1)D(0, 0, i+3)one unit left, even block: reset
A(2i+2, 0)haltno fuel, even block: F reads a 0 (halt_even)

So D(k, 0, z) first trades all of k for 3k ones, giving A(3k+3, z), and then halves. On the number k this is k → (3k+2)/2 for k even (fuel −1) and k → (3k+5)/2 for k odd (fuel −2). With u = k + 2 it is simply u → 3⌈u/2⌉, a close cousin of the maps behind the famous Hydra and Antihydra machines.

sections.heading: Every round replays the same sequence
html: A round starts at D(0, 0, z) with k = 0, so the sequence of k values is the same in every round: 0, 1, 4, 7, 13, 22, 34, 52, 79, ... Only the fuel z decides where the round stops. If it stops with k odd and the fuel exactly used up, the machine halts; otherwise the current k (about 1.5 times it) becomes the fuel of the next round, which is exponentially larger.

The fourth round needs about 1.5·1022 applications of the map to numbers with up to 1021 digits; nothing can compute that. For small fuel values a third of them end in a halt, which is why the machine most likely halts eventually, but nobody can say in which round.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,446 cells (34,595 left of the start, 9 right), with a density of 1s of 0.598.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A 3/2-Collatz-like map that burns a fuel counter: each round halts with chance about 1/3; it survived the rounds with fuel 5, 14 and 185, and the next has fuel 22,205,951,667,644,132,025,548.
